auxiliary_material: Mouse tumor models (B16-F0, B16-GMCSF, 4T1) demonstrating inosine plus ICB synergistic efficacy.
Chemical proteomics (LiP-SMap) identifying UBA6 as a direct binding target of inosine in tumor cells.
scRNA-seq analysis of immune cell populations in mouse tumors following inosine treatment.
In vitro co-culture assays showing inosine pretreatment of tumor cells enhances T cell-mediated killing.
Data on inosine derivative (isoprinosine) showing similar synergistic effects in mouse models.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this study to document the current standard of plasma-based metabolomic profiling in ICI trials and to highlight the absence of paired intratumoral metabolite data in major cohorts. Cite the inosine-UBA6 mechanism as a rationale for why intratumoral measurement would be valuable (since the target is tumor-intrinsic). Search for additional studies that specifically performed metabolomics on resected human tumor biopsies paired with plasma/fecal samples to address the TME quantification gap.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: This study does not report direct quantification of inosine or other metabolites within human tumor tissue (TME); measurements were restricted to plasma in humans and tumor tissue in mice. There is no comparison of human intratumoral metabolite concentrations versus fecal or plasma samples in ICI-treated patients. The specific methodology for human TME metabolite extraction and quantification remains unaddressed in this text.
useful_material: Human plasma metabolomics data from RCC patients (CheckMate 025 trial) treated with nivolumab, identifying inosine levels associated with overall survival.
Methodological detail on untargeted metabolomics using HPLC coupled with tripleTOF mass spectrometry on plasma samples.
Evidence linking gut microbiota depletion (antibiotics) to reduced inosine levels and compromised ICB efficacy in mouse models.
Clinical correlation of UBA6 protein expression (not metabolite) in human tumor tissues with ICB response.
Confirmation that inosine is a microbial-associated metabolite influencing ICI therapy outcomes.

record_identity.title: Inhibiting tumor cell-intrinsic UBA6 by inosine augments tumor immunogenicity

success_criteria_audit.gap_question: What specific methods or studies have attempted direct quantification of microbial metabolites (e.g., inosine, SCFAs) within the human tumor microenvironment (TME) versus fecal/plasma samples in the context of ICI therapy?
